# Neon Drift Racers

**Genre:** Arcade racing | **Developer:** Velocity Forge | **Released:** 2024 | **Price:** €19.99

Slide sideways through a rain-slicked neon metropolis in the arcade racer built around one thing: the perfect drift. Neon Drift Racers pairs a weight-transfer drift model — feather the throttle, flick the wheel, ride the slide — with an original synthwave soundtrack of 42 licensed-free tracks that syncs its beat drops to your corner exits.

## Features

- 14 circuits at launch, including Chromatic Bay, Sunset Loop, and the vertigo-inducing Skyline Spiral
- Championship mode with 8 cups, plus time trials with global leaderboards
- Drift ghosts: race your friends' best laps asynchronously
- 24 customizable cars across street, drift, and prototype classes
- Full soundtrack player in the garage

## System Requirements

- **OS:** 64-bit, 2018 or newer
- **CPU:** Quad-core 3.0 GHz
- **RAM:** 8 GB
- **GPU:** Vortex 2200 / TitanEdge 460 or better, 4 GB VRAM
- **Storage:** 25 GB
- Recommended for 144 fps: Vortex 3600 class GPU, 16 GB RAM

# Neon Drift Racers — Patch Notes

## v1.5 — 2025-09-30
- Added seasonal time trials with rotating track playlists and cosmetic rewards
- Drift ghost sharing: export a ghost link to friends outside your list
- Minor audio mixing fixes on Harbor Straight

## v1.4 — 2025-05-08
- **Stability:** Fixed a memory leak in the replay recorder (introduced in v1.3) that caused crashes to desktop and mid-race freezes, most frequently in the Midnight Interchange tunnel section
- **Stability:** Fixed a hang on the loading screen when the replay cache exceeded 2 GB
- Re-enabled automatic replay saving (disabled as a workaround in v1.3.1)
- Added crash telemetry opt-in to catch regressions faster

## v1.3.1 — 2025-03-02 (hotfix)
- Reduced the frequency of post-race crashes reported since v1.3
- Temporarily disabled automatic replay saving while we investigate the root cause

## v1.3 — 2025-02-11
- Two new tracks: Midnight Interchange and Harbor Straight
- New replay system with cinematic cameras and photo mode integration
- Drift ghosts now record full input data

## v1.2 — 2024-11-20
- Tuned AI catch-up assist on Expert difficulty (further tuning planned)
- Added photo mode
- Fixed collision jitter on Sunset Loop's banked hairpin

# Dungeon Sprouts

**Genre:** Cozy roguelite | **Developer:** Tiny Cauldron | **Released:** 2023 | **Price:** €14.99

Grow a tiny vegetable hero, descend into the friendliest dungeon ever composted, and lose track of an entire evening — again. Dungeon Sprouts wraps deep roguelite build-crafting in a warm blanket: when a run ends, the game plants a memorial flower where you fell, and your garden grows a little wiser.

## Features

- 60+ seed types with a synergy system that rewards absurd combinations
- Charming bosses, from knitting-obsessed Grandma Bramble to the towering Compost King
- Four biomes, including the Mossy Cellar and the Overgrown Attic
- Adoptable familiars (yes, the turnip can wear a hat)
- Meta-progression garden that remembers every run
- No fail states that punish; losing is just gardening

## System Requirements

- **OS:** 64-bit, 2016 or newer
- **CPU:** Dual-core 2.4 GHz
- **RAM:** 4 GB
- **GPU:** Any card from the last decade with 2 GB VRAM
- **Storage:** 3 GB
- Runs comfortably on low-end laptops and handhelds

# Dungeon Sprouts — Patch Notes

## v2.1 "Pockets & Compost" — 2025-06-17
- **Inventory increased from 12 to 20 slots** — you asked, we sewed pockets
- New compost system: convert duplicate seeds into Rich Soil, a currency that speeds up late-game greenhouse unlocks (targeting the endgame grind feedback)
- Greenhouse tier costs reduced by roughly 30%
- Familiars can now carry one item each

## v2.0 "Deep Roots" — 2024-09-05
- New biome: the Overgrown Attic
- New boss: the Compost King, assembled from everything you discarded during the run
- 12 new seed types and 3 new trinket slots
- Rebalanced late-game encounter tables

## v1.5 "Familiar Faces" — 2023-08-15
- Familiar cosmetics: hats, scarves, and tiny boots for every companion
- Quality of life: auto-sort button for the seed pouch, faster menu transitions
- Grandma Bramble now apologizes when she defeats you (it was rude before)

## v1.0 — 2023-03-21
- Launch release: three biomes, 40 seed types, 6 bosses, one very small turnip

# Star Salvage Crew

**Genre:** Co-op space sim | **Developer:** Orbital Labs | **Released:** 2025 | **Price:** €24.99

Somebody has to clean up the derelicts drifting through Sector 7 — and it pays best when nobody asks where the cargo came from. Star Salvage Crew is a 1–4 player salvage sim about cutting into dead ships, managing oxygen lines, and dragging contraband home before the reactor you assumed was cold proves otherwise.

## Features

- **Friend Pass:** one purchased copy lets up to three friends join for free
- Physically simulated cutting, breaching, and cargo handling
- Ten explorable wrecks at launch, from gutted freighters to the flooded research vessel Anemone
- Ship upgrades: better haulers, longer O2 lines, quieter engines
- Proximity voice chat with vacuum muffling — atmosphere is the whole point
- Best played with 3 friends; solo mode available with drone assistant

## System Requirements

- **OS:** 64-bit, 2019 or newer
- **CPU:** Six-core 3.2 GHz
- **RAM:** 16 GB
- **GPU:** Vortex 4600 / TitanEdge 900, 6 GB VRAM
- **Storage:** 40 GB
- **Network:** Broadband required for co-op

# Star Salvage Crew — Patch Notes

## v1.2 "Signal Lock" — 2026-01-09
- **Netcode overhaul:** movement and interaction are now server-authoritative, eliminating most desync and rubber-banding
- **Session reconnect:** if your connection drops, rejoin the same session within 10 minutes with inventory intact
- **Host migration:** if the host leaves or crashes, the session now transfers to another crew member instead of ending
- Fixed items appearing duplicated between clients and then vanishing on sale

## v1.1 — 2025-07-24
- New wreck: the Anemone, a flooded research vessel with security drones
- Friend Pass expanded from 2 to 3 free guest slots
- First round of desync mitigation: interpolation smoothing, cargo state reconciliation (further work ongoing)
- Voice chat vacuum muffling improvements

## v1.0.2 — 2025-03-18 (hotfix)
- Fixed a frequent disconnect when crossing airlock transitions with held cargo
- Patched a duplicate-salvage sale exploit
- Reduced connection timeouts during extraction sequences

## v1.0 — 2025-02-27
- Launch release: eight wrecks, four-player co-op, Friend Pass

# Castle Contractors

**Genre:** Building sim | **Developer:** Drawbridge Digital | **Released:** 2024 | **Price:** €29.99

You're not a king. You're the contractor kings call when they want a keep by Michaelmas and the moat dug by Tuesday. Castle Contractors is a physics-first medieval building sim where every wall bears real load — design it wrong and the collapse will show you exactly which stone betrayed you.

## Features

- Free-form construction: towers, gatehouses, banquet halls, regrettable balconies
- Structural physics with real load paths; collapses propagate believably
- Siege testing mode: bombard your own designs with catapults to find the weak points
- Contract campaign with 30 commissions, including the Baron's Folly chain
- Peasant workforce simulation with schedules, moods, and complaints
- Sandbox mode with unlimited stone

## System Requirements

- **OS:** 64-bit, 2019 or newer
- **CPU:** Eight-core 3.4 GHz (physics-heavy)
- **RAM:** 16 GB, 32 GB recommended for builds over 1,000 pieces
- **GPU:** Nova X1 / Vortex 4600, 6 GB VRAM
- **Storage:** 35 GB
- Note: very large castles are CPU- and GPU-intensive; see patch notes for ongoing optimization work

# Castle Contractors — Patch Notes

## v1.3 "Master Builder" — 2026-03-20
- **UI overhaul:** doors, windows, and stairs now place in one click from a persistent hotbar
- Radial build wheel remembers your last selection
- Blueprint sharing: export and import castle designs
- Full input rebinding
- First pass on distant-structure imposters; a full level-of-detail system remains in development

## v1.2 "Optimization Pass" — 2025-05-29
- **Performance:** instanced rendering for repeated pieces — up to 2x frame rate in castles over 1,000 pieces
- **Performance:** peasant pathfinding now batched; large workforces no longer cause rhythmic stutter at shift change
- Reduced physics solver cost for static, settled structures
- Known issue: frame dips during large collapses are expected and under investigation

## v1.1 — 2024-10-16
- New contract chain: the Baron's Folly (5 commissions with an unreliable client)
- Siege testing mode added to all completed contracts
- Partial fix for stutter when peasants gather in the bailey
- Fixed tapestries incorrectly counting as load-bearing (existing saves keep their tapestry physics until rebuilt)

## v1.0 — 2024-05-30
- Launch release: contract campaign, sandbox mode, collapse physics

# Pixel Pirates Online

**Genre:** MMO naval combat | **Developer:** Kraken Interactive | **Released:** 2022 | **Price:** Free to play

Hoist the colors in a shared-world pirate MMO where the wind is real, the broadsides are earned, and every ship needs a crew that can actually talk to each other. Pixel Pirates Online is built around 4-player crewed vessels: helm, sails, cannons, repairs — coordinate or sink.

## Features

- Crewed ship combat for up to 4 players per vessel, from sloops to galleons
- Living ocean with wind simulation, storms, and the whirlpool event the Kraken's Maw
- Open-sea PvP, trade routes, and tavern shanties
- Seasonal content, including the Sea Serpent Season battle pass
- Progression: earn sails, cannons, and cosmetics through play or the in-game Gem Shop
- Free to play; optional Deluxe Charter subscription

## System Requirements

- **OS:** 64-bit, 2016 or newer
- **CPU:** Quad-core 2.8 GHz
- **RAM:** 8 GB
- **GPU:** TitanEdge 500 or better, 3 GB VRAM
- **Storage:** 20 GB
- **Network:** Broadband required; persistent online world

# Pixel Pirates Online — Patch Notes

## v4.1 "Event Horizons" — 2025-11-05
- Event weekends now run on dedicated high-capacity servers
- **Priority boarding:** Deluxe Charter subscribers skip the standard login queue during peak hours
- New cosmetic line in the Gem Shop: Ghostfire sail set

## v4.0 "The Admiral's Vault" — 2025-03-12
- New feature: Vault Crates — randomized armament rewards, including the Ghost Cannon and Serpent Chaser lines with unique stat profiles
- Gem bundle pricing restructured; conversion rates updated
- Vault-exclusive armaments are not obtainable through gameplay progression
- Balance: legacy cannons adjusted to make room for the new armament tiers

## v3.5 "Sea Serpent Season" — 2024-06-19
- Introducing the seasonal battle pass: 60 tiers of sails, figureheads, and emotes
- Daily streak quests grant bonus pass progress; streaks reset after 48 hours of inactivity
- Pass tiers expire at season end
- New event: the Sea Serpent surfaces in open water every 3 hours

## v3.0 — 2023-08-02
- Gem Shop expanded beyond cosmetics: XP boosts, repair kits, and fast-travel charters now available
- New trade routes in the southern archipelago

## v2.0 — 2023-01-20
- Server capacity doubled in response to launch-window login queues
- Queue position and estimated wait now displayed on the login screen

# Kernel Panic

**Genre:** Hacking roguelike | **Developer:** Null Pointer Games | **Released:** 2025 | **Price:** €12.99

You are a rogue process inside a dying machine, and your only weapon is the shell. Kernel Panic is a turn-based roguelike played entirely through a working command line: navigate directories as dungeon floors, grep ghosts out of log files, pipe enemies into /dev/null, and pray your fingers don't typo under pressure — permadeath doesn't care that you meant grep.

## Features

- Real shell mechanics: pipes, redirection, grep, chmod, cron, and man pages, all load-bearing
- Procedurally generated filesystems with seeded runs and daily challenges
- Daemon bosses, including the Kernel and the schedule-reading Cron Reaper
- Practice Sandbox mode: a consequence-free shell with a searchable in-game manual
- Artifacts that upgrade your shell itself, like tab completion and command history
- Chiptune soundtrack that compiles surprisingly hard

## System Requirements

- **OS:** 64-bit, 2014 or newer
- **CPU:** Dual-core 2.0 GHz
- **RAM:** 4 GB
- **GPU:** Anything that renders a terminal font
- **Storage:** 800 MB
- **Keyboard:** Mandatory. Sorry, controllers.

# Kernel Panic — Patch Notes

## v1.2 "Training Wheels, Sort Of" — 2025-11-13
- **New: Practice Sandbox** — a consequence-free shell where death just respawns you; built in direct response to feedback about the learning curve
- **New: in-game manual** — searchable man pages for every command, no more alt-tabbing to a wiki
- Optional hint daemon: whispers a suggested command after three deaths on the same floor (off by default, purists)
- First-run flow now offers Sandbox before your first real descent

## v1.1 — 2025-08-27
- New artifact: tab completion (floor six loot pool) — dramatically speeds up experienced runs
- Difficulty smoothing on floors one through three: fewer ambushes, more readable log clues
- Cron Reaper boss rework: its spawn schedule is now a real, readable crontab you can edit mid-fight if you're fast
- Fixed a crash when piping more than 256 enemies in a single command (we were impressed, though)

## v1.0 — 2025-06-05
- Launch release: 12 filesystem depths, 9 daemon bosses, seeded runs, daily challenges
- Known omission acknowledged in reviews: no tutorial. The machine does not explain itself. (See v1.2.)

# Haunted Spreadsheet

**Genre:** Horror comedy sim | **Developer:** Cursed Cell Studio | **Released:** 2024 | **Price:** €9.99

It's 5:47 PM. Everyone else has gone home. The quarterly budget file you opened has 13 sheets, and you only made 12. Haunted Spreadsheet is a short-form horror comedy played entirely inside an eerily convincing office spreadsheet: audit the numbers, answer the cell comments, and try not to look at F13.

## Features

- A complete horror story told through formulas, macros, and passive-aggressive cell comments
- The pivot-table jump scare (we will not elaborate)
- The macro seance: contact the intern who never logged off
- Fiscal Year of Fear: a free post-launch chapter featuring the year-end audit
- New Game Plus with three additional endings and one secret ending hidden behind a formula
- Main story: roughly 2 hours; completionist runs considerably longer since the free update

## System Requirements

- **OS:** 64-bit, 2012 or newer
- **CPU:** Anything that can open a spreadsheet
- **RAM:** 4 GB
- **GPU:** Integrated graphics fine
- **Storage:** 2 GB
- **Headphones:** strongly recommended after sunset

# Haunted Spreadsheet — Patch Notes

## v1.2 "Fiscal Year of Fear" — 2025-10-24
- **Free new chapter:** the year-end audit — roughly one additional hour of story, added in response to feedback about the game's length
- **New Game Plus:** three new endings that recontextualize the first playthrough
- One secret ending, unlocked by a formula the community will find eventually (no hints)
- New scare: we fixed the thing in the footer. It is not fixed. Do not read the footer.

## v1.1 — 2025-01-17
- Fixed a softlock in the macro seance when players deleted the intern's sheet mid-ritual
- Added speedrun timer with in-game splits per sheet
- Accessibility: scare intensity slider, reduced-flash mode, dyslexia-friendly font option
- The pivot-table now waits until you are comfortable. This made it worse. Intended.

## v1.0 — 2024-10-01
- Launch release: 13 sheets, one intern, zero survivors of the Q3 budget review

# Orbit Fall

**Genre:** Physics platformer | **Price:** €7.99 | **Released:** 2023 | **Developer:** Weightless Whale

Gravity is not your enemy. It's your only friend. Orbit Fall is a precision platformer built on a fully deterministic physics engine: momentum, arc, and orbital pull behave identically on every attempt, so mastery is always possible and every fall is a lesson. Fling yourself between gravity wells, thread the Slingshot Gauntlet, and survive the magnetic fury of Magnetron Prime on your way through the shattered moons of Kepler Junction.

## Features

- 120 hand-tuned levels across six gravity zones, including the Tidal Locks and Gravity Well 7
- Deterministic physics — same input, same result, every time. Beloved by speedrunners.
- Global leaderboards with ghost replays and a daily challenge run
- Adaptive soundtrack that intensifies the longer you fall
- Full controller support with per-axis deadzone calibration (added in v1.5.0)

## System Requirements

- **OS:** Windows 10 64-bit
- **CPU:** Dual-core 2.4 GHz
- **RAM:** 4 GB
- **GPU:** Any card with 1 GB VRAM; integrated graphics supported
- **Storage:** 900 MB

# Orbit Fall — Patch Notes

## v1.5.0 — 2026-02-10

Controller support is officially out of beta.

- Fixed gamepad detection failures on setups with multiple USB input devices; hot-plugging now works without restarting the game
- Added per-axis deadzone sliders and three response-curve presets (Linear, Classic, Feather)
- Input polling decoupled from vsync — measured input latency reduced by roughly 45 ms on 60 Hz displays
- Added an in-game input latency test in Options > Calibration
- New default framerate cap (240) to prevent frame-pacing judder on high-refresh monitors

## v1.4.2 (beta branch) — 2024-01-22

- Experimental gamepad support available via the `input-beta` opt-in branch
- Known issues: analog deadzone behaves inconsistently on some third-party pads; detection may fail after suspend/resume
- Fixed a physics edge case where wall-bounces at the apex of Gravity Well 7 lost momentum

## v1.2.1 — 2023-10-05

- Added two checkpoints to Gravity Well 7 following community feedback
- Magnetron Prime: reduced projectile density in phase two by 15%
- Added a "Steady Orbit" assist toggle (slows time by 10%, disables leaderboards)

## v1.0.3 — 2023-08-20

- Launch-week stability fixes
- Known issue: some players report gamepads not being detected at all. We are investigating; current workaround is keyboard input. We hear you — proper controller support is our top priority.

# Moth Light

**Genre:** Metroidvania | **Price:** €17.99 | **Released:** 2025 | **Developer:** Lantern Collective

Follow the last lantern-bearer into a kingdom that forgot the sun. Moth Light is a hand-drawn metroidvania about grief, light, and the things that gather around it. Every frame of animation is drawn by hand; every corridor of the Wax Cathedral, Cinder Hollow, and the Gloaming is painted like a storybook you shouldn't have opened. Beneath the beauty waits a mournful cello score and a story that has left even hardened genre veterans in tears.

## Features

- Fully hand-drawn art and animation — over 14,000 individual frames
- A haunting orchestral score built around solo cello, recorded live
- Duel-like boss encounters, including Mother Pyralis and the Chandler
- Deep movement kit with ability-gated exploration and sequence-break potential
- Bench-warp fast travel network and customizable map pins (expanded in update 1.1)
- 20+ hour story with a fully voiced ending sequence

## System Requirements

- **OS:** Windows 10 64-bit
- **CPU:** Quad-core 2.8 GHz
- **RAM:** 8 GB
- **GPU:** 2 GB VRAM (1050-class or better)
- **Storage:** 6 GB

# Moth Light — Patch Notes

## v1.1.0 "Wayfinder" — 2026-03-12

Our biggest update yet, focused on the number one piece of community feedback: navigation.

- Added custom map pins — place up to 30 markers with six icon types
- Redesigned the map legend; room outlines now distinguish visited, cleared, and secret-remaining states
- The first bench-warp (fast travel) unlock moved from the Gloaming to early Cinder Hollow — roughly three hours earlier in a typical playthrough
- Bench-warp costs reduced by 50%; warping is now free after collecting the Compass Sigil
- Corridor signposts added at seven major junctions

## v1.0.3 — 2025-09-18

- Smoothed the difficulty spike in the mid-Gloaming gauntlet; enemy density reduced
- Fixed Mother Pyralis occasionally skipping her lullaby phase transition
- Fixed a soft-lock when quitting during the Chandler's second phase
- Audio: fixed cello theme cutting out when entering the Wax Cathedral from the east lift

## v1.0.1 — 2025-04-10

- Launch fixes: resolved a rare crash on ultrawide displays
- Fixed collectible counter displaying 99% at 100% completion
- Minor dialogue typo corrections

# Turbo Goat Simulator 9

**Genre:** Meme sandbox | **Price:** €6.99 | **Released:** 2024 | **Developer:** Chaos Pasture

The ninth entry in a series that has never once been asked for. You are a goat. The town of Bleatsburg is legally unprepared for you. Headbutt, lick, drag, and ragdoll your way through a physics engine we describe, with full sincerity, as "load-bearing duct tape." Clip through Mayor Crumb. Ascend via the trampoline church. Strap on a jetpack and ruin a wedding. The bugs are not mistakes — they are the content, and we patch around the funny ones very carefully.

## Features

- Fully destructible(ish) open town of Bleatsburg with five districts
- Industrial-strength tongue physics: lick it, drag it, regret it
- Jetpacks, trampolines, and the fan-favorite Goatnado event mode (v9.3)
- Challenge checklist and unlockable mutators for goal-oriented chaos (added in v9.1)
- Couch co-op party modes for up to four goats (v9.4)

## System Requirements

- **OS:** Windows 10 64-bit
- **CPU:** Dual-core 2.6 GHz
- **RAM:** 8 GB
- **GPU:** 2 GB VRAM
- **Storage:** 4 GB
- **Dignity:** none required

# Turbo Goat Simulator 9 — Patch Notes

## v9.4 — 2026-04-01

- Added couch co-op party modes: Goal Goat (football, sort of), Crumb Chase, and Demolition Derby
- Up to four goats on one screen; frame rate is now a shared responsibility
- Fixed a bug where the ice cream truck could achieve escape velocity. Re-added it as a mutator called "Escape Velocity"

## v9.3 "Goatnado" — 2025-07-15

- New event mode: Goatnado. Sixty goats. One tornado. Zero apologies.
- Performance warning: Goatnado is not optimized. It will never be optimized. This is a promise.
- Mayor Crumb now screams in slow motion when airborne for more than four seconds

## v9.1 "Bleatsburg Bash" — 2024-11-20

We heard the feedback that the fun runs out after a few hours. This one is for you.

- New district: the Marina, featuring a fully lickable ferry
- Added a 120-item challenge checklist with unlockable mutators (low gravity, rubber town, infinite tongue)
- 40 new physics props, including a grand piano and a portable trampoline
- Fixed goats phasing through the town hall floor. Community response was negative, so we un-fixed it.

## v9.0.2 — 2024-05-05

- Fixed a crash when licking the mayor during the ferris wheel cutscene
- Deliberately did not fix the funeral launch exploit
- Reduced load times by 30% so you can get to the nonsense faster

# Chess Royale 100

**Genre:** Strategy battle royale | **Price:** Free to play | **Released:** 2023 | **Developer:** Checkmate Cloud

One hundred players. One colossal board. One crown. Chess Royale 100 drops you onto a giant shared board where every player commands their own army in real time — and the board itself is shrinking. As the circle closes, entire files and ranks collapse into the void, forcing sprawling positional wars into desperate final-circle knife fights. Outlast, outthink, and claim the crown while 99 defeated ghosts spectate your endgame.

## Features

- 100-player simultaneous chess with a shrinking board and a shared final circle
- Ranked crown ladder with seasonal placement and spectator ghost mode
- Blitz Island limited-time mode: faster circles, no takebacks, pure chaos
- Fortress anti-cheat with server-side move analysis and regular ban waves (v2.0+)
- Replay review and community reporting tribunal (v2.5)
- Free forever: cosmetics only, no pay-to-win

## System Requirements

- **OS:** Windows 10 64-bit / any modern browser client
- **CPU:** Dual-core 2.0 GHz
- **RAM:** 4 GB
- **GPU:** Integrated graphics supported
- **Network:** Broadband required
- **Storage:** 1.5 GB

# Chess Royale 100 — Patch Notes

## v2.5 — 2026-04-22

- Added the Replay Tribunal: flagged games are anonymized and reviewed by high-rank community panels; verdicts feed the ban system
- Matchmaking Rating v3: placement matches now seed by measured move accuracy instead of win count — new players should no longer meet thousand-win veterans in their first sessions
- Bot backfill now clearly labels bot opponents in the post-game summary
- Fortress engine-detection model retrained; detection latency down from days to hours

## v2.3 — 2025-05-14

- Matchmaking rework: rank bands tightened, smurf-detection heuristics added
- Bot backfill reduced by 60% below rank 5; queue times may increase slightly at off-peak hours
- Fixed a bug where the same three bot profiles appeared repeatedly in consecutive lobbies
- Cosmetic crown-shard drop rate doubled

## v2.0 "Fortress" — 2024-08-19

Our largest integrity update ever.

- Introduced Fortress: server-side move analysis that flags statistically inhuman play across a match, not single moves
- First ban wave completed: 14,182 accounts removed
- Report flow shortened to two clicks; reporters now receive outcome notifications
- Known limitation: detection favors precision over speed; sophisticated cheaters may take multiple games to flag. Ongoing work.

## v1.4 — 2023-12-06

- Bot backfill tuning: bots now blunder at human-plausible rates (we are aware this sentence is funny)
- Queue time improvements at low ranks
- Fixed final-circle draw conditions when both kings fall into the void simultaneously

# Silent Depths

**Genre:** Survival horror | **Price:** €21.99 | **Released:** 2025 | **Developer:** Abyssal Point

Eleven kilometers down, the research station Meridian went silent. You are the one they sent to find out why. Silent Depths is a survival horror game about pressure — the hull's, and yours. Navigate flooded decks by sonar, ration flares and suit fuel, and listen: the anglerkin hunt by sound, and the Tidewalker never stopped hunting at all. Binaural audio design means you will hear things breathing before you ever see them. Most players finish with the lights on. Nobody finishes with headphones off.

## Features

- Award-caliber binaural sound design; headphones strongly recommended
- Sonar-based navigation through the Meridian, the Brinefall, and the trench beyond
- Survival systems: flares, suit fuel, oxygen, and a save network of pressure lockers
- Story told through crew logs — quiet, devastating, fully voiced
- Manual save slots with backup rotation (added in v1.2)

## System Requirements

- **OS:** Windows 10/11 64-bit
- **CPU:** 6-core 3.2 GHz
- **RAM:** 16 GB
- **GPU (minimum):** 8 GB VRAM — with texture streaming on Medium (improved in v1.2)
- **GPU (recommended):** 12 GB VRAM for High textures at 1080p and above
- **Storage:** 45 GB SSD required

# Silent Depths — Patch Notes

## v1.2.0 — 2026-01-15

This is the update we owed you.

- **Save system rewritten.** Save serialization is now atomic: a crash, alt-tab, or power loss during an autosave can no longer corrupt the file. Internal testing and beta-branch telemetry show zero corruptions across 40,000 save events.
- Added three manual save slots with automatic backup rotation; the last two autosaves are also kept as recoverable backups
- Corrupted saves from earlier versions: the launcher now attempts recovery from backup fragments — roughly 70% of affected files are restorable
- **Performance:** texture streaming pipeline rebuilt. VRAM usage reduced by ~30%; zone-transition hitching eliminated on 8 GB cards at Medium textures
- Minimum spec guidance updated to be honest about 8 GB vs 12 GB VRAM behavior

## v1.1.0 — 2025-09-03

- Autosave mitigation: saves now double-buffer to a temporary file before committing (reduces, but does not eliminate, corruption — full fix in development)
- Fixed the crash on Deck C of the Meridian tied to the ventilation cutscene
- Performance pass on the Brinefall approach; average fps up 12% on 8 GB cards
- Tidewalker chase: added a checkpoint before the flooded stairwell

## v1.0.4 — 2025-04-18

- Hotfix for the most common Deck C crash
- Fixed anglerkin audio positioning being mirrored on some 7.1 headsets
- Reduced flare drop variance in the early decks

# Bureau of Time

**Genre:** Detective adventure | **Price:** €18.99 | **Released:** 2024 | **Developer:** Clockwise Bureau

At 4:17 every afternoon, the city resets — and only you and Inspector Vell remember. Bureau of Time is a time-loop detective adventure where the same ten minutes hide an entire conspiracy. Interrogate suspects who don't know they've answered before, chase evidence through the Records Annex, and rearrange the case in your head loop after loop until it finally, terribly, makes sense. The ending has become something of a legend among players — the community's one rule is that nobody spoils it.

## Features

- Time-loop investigation: replay the 4:17 reset with everything you've learned
- Branching interrogations with a fully reactive deduction board
- Handcrafted puzzles, from the telegraph cipher to the pneumatic mail sorter
- Consultant Mode: optional tiered hints for stuck detectives (added in v1.4)
- 15–20 hour story with a twist ending players refuse to spoil
- Loop-skip and chapter select after first completion

## System Requirements

- **OS:** Windows 10 64-bit
- **CPU:** Quad-core 2.6 GHz
- **RAM:** 8 GB
- **GPU:** 3 GB VRAM
- **Storage:** 12 GB

# Bureau of Time — Patch Notes

## v1.4.0 — 2026-03-20

- **New: Consultant Mode.** An optional, three-tier hint system — a nudge, a lead, and a full solution — available from the pause menu. Off by default; using it disables nothing and judges no one.
